instructions: Return exactly one JSON object with exactly one string key named module. No Markdown fences or text outside JSON. The UTF-8 JSON output must be at most 16384 bytes. module must define coalesce(ranges: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]. Input must be a list. Each pair may be a length-two list or tuple; both endpoints must have exact type int (not bool) and start < end. Invalid input must raise ValueError. Valid inputs are half-open intervals: return the sorted maximal union, merging overlap and touching endpoints, as a list of two-int tuples. Do not mutate input. Empty list returns an empty list. No dependencies, file/network/process access, API calls, tests, README or application scaffolding. Example: [[4, 7], [1, 4], [9, 11]] returns [(1, 7), (9, 11)]. Restricted grammar restricted-python-v1: the module contains only an optional docstring and one undecorated synchronous coalesce function; optional nested helper functions have unique names and plain positional parameters without defaults. At most 8 functions, 2000 AST nodes and depth 40. No imports, classes, decorators, reflection, IO, lambdas, try/except, globals, nonlocals, private/dunder names or indirect calls. Allowed builtins: len, type, isinstance, int, bool, list, tuple, range, sorted, enumerate, zip, reversed, min, max, sum, abs, all, any, ValueError. type takes one argument only; ValueError takes no argument or one literal string. Only direct list method calls append, extend, sort, copy, pop are allowed; no other attribute access or saved bound methods. Supported statements: plain assignments, augmented assignments, return, if, for, while, break, continue, pass, raise ValueError; expressions include lists, tuples, subscripts/slices, comparisons, boolean/arithmetic operations (+ - * // %), conditional expressions, list comprehensions and generator expressions. No rebinding builtin or function names in any parameter, assignment, loop or comprehension. Function calls may target only these builtins or declared functions; helpers take positional args. sorted/sort allow key as a declared helper and reverse as literal bool; enumerate allows start; no other keywords or argument expansion. Annotations may use only int, bool, list, tuple, None and nested list/tuple subscriptions; they are removed before execution. Grammar-rejected code is ungradable; the subset will not be broadened after a trial.
